decisions.approvalNote: The user explicitly approved Option A: a bounded session-scoped notification center backed by authoritative model-download task lifecycle state.
decisions.context: The choice determines whether download progress is truthful and cross-page, whether notification history survives restart, and whether this remains a renderer presentation feature or becomes a new persisted platform service.

consequences: Transient toasts stay for five seconds and fade, while the dropdown keeps bounded session history and active work until dismissed or terminally handled.
Model downloads can show queued/running state and provider-reported percentage when available, with an honest indeterminate state otherwise.
Desktop and thin client share behavior and presentation while host-specific clients retain transport ownership.
Contextual field validation, blocking diagnostics, loading/empty state, and security/readiness guidance remain inline rather than disappearing after five seconds.
options.label: Session center with authoritative tasks
options.summary: Create one bounded session-scoped shared notification center for desktop and thin client, migrate transient page/tab outcomes into it, retain current-session history, and promote model downloads into the existing authoritative runtime-task lifecycle so queued, running, progress, failure, cancellation, and completion remain visible across navigation.
tradeoffs: Provides the requested real queue and progress instead of inventing percentages in the renderer.

Requires a coordinated runtime contract, application, adapter, API/IPC/preload/client, and UI change plus canonical architecture/ADR reconciliation because model downloads are not currently a shared TaskType.
Avoids a new notification database and retention policy; ordinary notification history resets on app reload while authoritative active tasks can be recovered from the task source.

consequences: The top-bar center solves visibility for saves and errors but only partially satisfies the requested download-progress behavior.
Downloads display indeterminate activity until the existing request returns.
A later roadmap would still need to promote downloads into authoritative task contracts.
options.label: Session center with UI-only activity
options.summary: Create the same session-scoped center and migrate transient messages, but leave model download APIs blocking and represent only renderer-known queued/downloading/completed states without a shared task identity or authoritative percentage.
tradeoffs: Smaller and lower-risk cross-layer implementation because runtime contracts and transports remain unchanged.
Cannot truthfully provide a real multi-download queue, percentage, recovery after navigation/reload, or cancellation; the UI only knows that a request is pending.
Feature-owned request state can drift from backend work after transport interruption or component unmount.

consequences: Notification history and unread state survive restart and could be shared across clients.
The implementation becomes a platform capability rather than a shared UI feature.
A dedicated persistence/security architecture decision and broader qualification would be required before implementation.
options.label: Durable platform inbox and task stream
options.summary: Create a persisted server/desktop notification inbox with read state, retention, cross-session history, and task-event delivery, and also promote model downloads into durable task records.
tradeoffs: Provides restart persistence and could support future multi-device delivery.
Introduces new persistence schema, retention/deletion, authorization, tenancy, synchronization, audit, transport, and migration decisions far beyond the requested in-app visibility feature.
Carries the highest disclosure and stale-data risk because user-visible diagnostics are stored durably.

constraints: Put the notification bell immediately before Settings in both app shells and render its anchored panel below the sticky header at the content area's top-right.
Use one shared host-neutral notification model, provider, presenter, icon, styles, and behavior; app shells may own platform wiring but must not fork the interaction contract.
Transient page or tab action outcomes appear for five seconds and then fade out, while the dropdown retains a bounded session history until the user clears or dismisses it.

Do not remove contextual field validation, modal/build diagnostics, loading and empty states, blocking readiness or security guidance, or inline progress controls whose local context is required to complete the task; migrate only duplicative transient action messages and page/tab notices.

Long-running activity must be derived from authoritative task or operation state rather than logs, labels, timers, or renderer-invented percentages; unknown or unavailable progress remains explicitly indeterminate.
Scope every workspace-owned notification and task to the authoritative active workspace and prevent stale workspace messages from being presented as current.

Bound message length, history count, live-region announcements, active task count, polling, and retained metadata; never display secrets, raw provider payloads, private prompts, local paths, stack traces, or raw logs.
Preserve the existing dirty System Builder changes and reconcile the overlapping SystemBuilderWorkspace transient-message migration without overwriting the prior chatbot build fix.
Add no dependency unless current platform primitives prove insufficient, and keep notification presentation out of domain/application business logic.
Use focused tests during each approved increment and run applicable documentation, architecture, agent-support, server, thin-client, desktop, and repository-wide gates once at the increment boundary.

A critical blocking validation, security, or readiness message disappears after five seconds because all contextual messages are removed indiscriminately.
Out-of-order task updates regress progress, revive completed work, or present a failed download as successful.

discovery.summary: Desktop and thin-client already share the same sticky shell structure and shared shell styling, but each shell independently renders only navigation and Settings actions. Transient action outcomes are fragmented across feature-local strings, view-state records, notices, alerts, and status paragraphs, so messages can scroll out of view and often remain indefinitely. Long-running work is also fragmented: the shared runtime task registry carries bounded progress for several task types, while model-management downloads currently block their API/IPC request until a private Python ensure-model-download task completes; only Dataset Preparation derives model-download percentages by parsing runtime logs. A truthful cross-page queue therefore requires an explicit choice between UI-only indeterminate activity and elevating model downloads into an authoritative public task lifecycle.

plan.summary: Implement Increment 1 in three cohesive chunks: establish the bounded shared notification experience in both shells; promote model downloads into the shared task lifecycle with safe application finalization; then expose and consume that lifecycle across API/IPC clients and model UI before running the increment completion gates.

risks: The current download result includes a local path; returning generic task data to API, IPC, preload, or notification UI would disclose host filesystem detail.
Changing model.download from completion to task acceptance can break Dataset Preparation and other callers unless renderer clients receive an explicit short-polling compatibility helper.
Concurrent status and list reads can register the same completed model more than once unless finalization is idempotent and guarded by one shared promise/result.

The worker does not expose a list endpoint, so authoritative navigation recovery must use bounded current-process registry records rather than inventing a renderer queue or broadening runtime topology.
Progress payloads contain provider-specific fields; mapping must allowlist bounded percentage/current/total/unit/message data instead of forwarding details wholesale.

Workspace switches, stale reads, and out-of-order polling can expose or regress another workspace's activity unless the application service verifies request ownership and the renderer store enforces monotonic terminal states.
Timer, listener, polling, and object-URL style cleanup defects could leak resources across lazy page remounts; provider and client teardown need deterministic tests.
The existing uncommitted System Builder changes overlap only with Increment 2 and must remain untouched during Increment 1.

research.summary: The sticky desktop and thin-client shells can share a provider, bell, anchored panel, and toast viewport from modules/ui/shared without changing route authority. The Python worker already runs ensure-model-download asynchronously and emits bounded structured file/byte progress, but the Node Python client currently hides that lifecycle behind polling and the generic adapter neither maps the task type nor lists current-process records. The smallest authoritative path is to add model-download to the shared TaskType, let the Python registry adapter start/read/cancel and retain bounded current-process records for listing, and add a model application task service that owns workspace-scoped request descriptors, exactly-once model registration, and sanitized projections. API/IPC/preload clients can then use short start/read/list/cancel calls, while renderer convenience code may poll those operations without holding transport requests open.

increments.rollback: Disable the shell activity projection and remove the additive model-download lifecycle operations together, allowing the existing bounded synchronous model download path to remain temporarily available only if its current authorization, workspace, sanitization, and timeout controls are unchanged. Do not fabricate progress, fall back to log parsing, expose raw runtime payloads, or mark incomplete downloads successful.

risks: Blanket removal of role=status or role=alert would erase contextual loading, validation, build, readiness, task-progress, and retry feedback.
Feature components are frequently tested outside the application root, so the migration publisher must be safe without a provider while remaining mandatory in production composition.
Rendering-driven publication can duplicate messages across harmless rerenders unless it tracks message transitions and uses bounded deduplication keys.
The current dirty System Builder change overlaps its top-level error and notice block; edits must be surgical and preserve the chatbot interaction reconciliation behavior and tests.
Raw action failures can contain local paths or transport details; every migrated producer must still pass through the shared sanitizer and retain only bounded copy.
Workspace-scoped producers must pass authoritative workspace ids so a switch cannot expose stale notifications from another workspace.
